edbDesc: Abnormally high rise of a liquid and its penetration into capillary channels due to a high-intensity ultrasound field. Caused by the collapse of cavitation bubbles at the capillary inlet. A collaping bubble generates a liquid microjet, the penetration of which into capillary channel causes the height increment of the capillary liquid column. Summation of such increments lies behind the increase of a height and a velocity of the liquid rise in a capillary under the ultrasound action.
title: Ultrasonic capillary effect
description: Strong ultrasound makes a liquid climb far higher and faster up a thin tube or into fine pores than it normally would, driven by bubbles collapsing at the tube's mouth. Konovalov reported it in 1961, and it's used to drive liquids deep into porous parts and narrow gaps.
effect: ultrasound drives a liquid far higher up narrow channels
usedIn: Ultrasonic impregnation of porous castings and coil windings
strength: Under strong ultrasound a liquid rises in a fine tube several times higher than by capillary action alone.
pickWhy: Borderline: Specific named effect with a clear job (pushing liquid into pores), but I'm unsure of the date and the size of the effect, and it could instead go on the Cavitation card (another batch).
